source_scope: Complete 188-line 2014 first-edition core extraction. No PDF, browsing, prior game knowledge, question set, key, reader answers or grades used.
verdict_basis: Material unsupported depleted-supply exception plus explicit omissions and smaller reference/wording issues. Unsupported does not mean independently disproven; this source does not establish the exception.

findings.claim: If fewer than three gem colors remain, take only as many different colors as remain.
findings.assessment: The source requires taking three different gems and separately gives the four-token prerequisite for taking two alike. It never supplies a depleted-supply exception for a one- or two-token different-color action. This materially changes which actions are legal. The audit does not claim this exception is independently proven false; it is not established by this source.
findings.recommended_change: Remove the exception or explicitly mark the situation unresolved by this extraction; do not invent the opposite ruling.

findings.claim: Public visibility of all held tokens is omitted.
findings.assessment: The source expressly requires tokens owned by a player to be visible to all players at all times. The summary covers public card values but never states this token rule.
findings.recommended_change: State that all held gem and gold tokens must remain visible to everyone.

findings.claim: The destination and orientation of an acquired noble tile are omitted.
findings.assessment: The source says the obtained noble tile is placed face-up in front of its recipient.
Ten is the component inventory. Only players plus one nobles are used; remaining tiles are removed. The earlier setup is correct but this quick-reference label conflicts with it.
findings.recommended_change: Use Noble tiles in box: 10 or Noble tiles in play: players + 1.

findings.claim: Card-level cost/point generalizations, printed corner positions, and exact 0–5 development-card prestige range.
findings.assessment: The extraction establishes counts, costs, bonuses, prestige and a four-point blue-bonus example. It does not establish the printed field positions, a five-point maximum or comparative cost/point distributions by level. The top-left bonus location cannot be verified from this text.
findings.recommended_change: Remove or mark these specifics unverified; retain the supported descriptions of cost, bonus and prestige.

findings.claim: Cards reserved from the top of a deck are never shown to other players.
findings.assessment: The source says a card drawn for reservation is not shown. Purchased cards must later display bonuses and prestige. In context the intended meaning is probably hidden while reserved, but never shown is too broad as a permanent restriction.
findings.recommended_change: Say drawn without revealing and hidden while reserved; purchased cards are displayed.

checked_claims.claim: Component inventory: 40 tokens, seven each of five gem colors, five gold; 90 developments split 40/30/20; ten nobles.
Shuffle decks separately, arrange increasing levels bottom to top, reveal four per level; shuffle nobles and reveal players plus one, remove leftovers; six sorted token piles.
Two players use four tokens per gem color and three nobles; three use five per color and four nobles; gold unchanged; four use full supply and five nobles.
Youngest starts; clockwise; exactly one of four actions per turn.
Take three different gem tokens, or two alike only when at least four of that color remain.
Gold cannot be taken through either ordinary gem-taking action.
checked_claims.qualification: Reserving is expressly the only way to get a gold token.

checked_claims.claim: Take fewer than three different gems when fewer colors remain.
checked_claims.qualification: Material unsupported legal-action exception; see F01.

checked_claims.claim: Reserve a face-up card or top card of any level without showing a blind draw; keep in hand, maximum three; no discarding; only holder may buy.
checked_claims.qualification: Never shown must be limited to reservation; see F06.

checked_claims.claim: Reserve takes one gold if available and is legal without gold.
Buy one face-up card or a card in own hand reserved on a previous turn.
Pay printed costs less bonuses; joker replaces any color; spent gems and gold return to middle supply.
Bonuses stack by color, persist for later purchases, can enable zero-token purchases and do not create tokens or change.
checked_claims.qualification: Source describes each acquired card contributing discounts, not card spending or physical token generation. No separate per-color cap is stated; finite card inventory still bounds accumulation.

checked_claims.claim: Purchased cards sorted by color and staggered with bonuses/prestige visible to all.
Immediately replace purchased or reserved face-up card from same level; depleted decks leave empty spaces.
At most ten tokens including gold at end of turn; return chosen excess including newly drawn tokens.
checked_claims.qualification: Source does not expressly sequence token returns before noble check. Summary sequence has no identified material effect because nobles use bonuses only.

checked_claims.claim: All held tokens visible at all times.
Check nobles at end of own turn; at least required bonuses only; automatic, not an action; at most one; choose if multiple; three points each.
checked_claims.qualification: Summary line 200 is read in the own-turn context expressly stated at line 135, not checking everyone after opponents turns.

checked_claims.claim: Unchosen qualifying nobles remain available for later turns.
checked_claims.qualification: Only selected tile is obtained; no discard of unchosen nobles is specified. Another player may obtain one in the meantime.

checked_claims.claim: Place acquired noble tile face-up in front of recipient.
Fifteen or more prestige triggers finishing current round for equal turns; highest prestige wins including nobles; fewest purchased developments breaks points tie.
checked_claims.qualification: Detailed end-game section resolves imprecise source overview at lines 51–52. Triggerer need not win. No further tiebreaker is specified by source or summary.

checked_claims.claim: Exact 0–5 prestige range, printed field locations and level-by-level cost/point distributions.
checked_claims.qualification: See F05. Text extraction cannot verify complete physical card layouts or distributions.

checked_claims.claim: Metadata: play time 30 minutes and exact player range 2–4.
checked_claims.qualification: Extraction includes rules for two and three and an explicit four-player example but no overall range or playing time. Designer and 2014 publication are supported at source lines 130, 134, 147.

source_limitations: Source does not resolve fewer-than-three-colors token taking, optional under-taking, passing, or a further tiebreak after equal points and equal purchased-card counts. This audit supplies no rulings on those cases.
Printed card layout and full card-value distributions cannot be verified from this extraction alone.
Administrative metadata and extraction-missing visual details are not treated as proven gameplay errors.
